discovery: Emergent magnetic monopoles and fractionalization in spin ice

nominees.name: Roderich Moessner
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for the Physics of Complex Systems, Dresden, Germany

motivation: In 2008 Castelnovo, Moessner and Sondhi showed that the elementary excitations of spin ice materials such as Dy2Ti2O7 and Ho2Ti2O7 are emergent magnetic monopoles: point-like sources of the H field that are deconfined, interact through a magnetic Coulomb law and carry a quantifiable magnetic charge. The idea, that a real crystal of ordinary magnetic moments can fractionalize into free magnetic charges moving in an emergent gauge field, gave a precise and testable picture of fractionalization in three dimensions. A wave of experiments confirmed its predictions: pinch-point and Dirac-string signatures seen in polarized neutron scattering, monopole dynamics and noise, 'magnetricity' in muon studies, and field-tuned Kasteleyn transitions. Their work created the field of emergent electrodynamics in frustrated magnets and continues to shape how we search for quantum spin liquids and gauge-field physics in materials.
